scene: Day 210, dusk at the bend of a two-lane road: Reed (blue-gray scarf, gray backpack) and Mara (purple forearm band, teal backpack, holding the red fuel can) stand on the grassy bank in the foreground, seen from behind and the side, holding hands. Down the road, dark smooth units line the verge with joined circles glowing at their bases, leading to the gas station from episode one: red-and-gray canopy fully lit, pump displays glowing, shop lights on behind a cracked window, nobody inside. The sky is empty, deep blue, with no ship. What makes it scary: the station has been dark since day seven, and tonight every light in it is on, as if it is waiting for them.

Day 198, a country road at dusk in the last of the snow: Reed (blue-gray scarf) pulls a child's wooden sled loaded with bags and the red fuel can; Mara (purple forearm band) stands beside him, both frozen mid-step and staring. Every dark unit along the verge, across the fields and on distant roads to the horizon has lit up at once, joined circles glowing pale at every base like a giant map of light. The sky above is empty. What makes it scary: the ship has gone, but every light in the country just switched on together.
